newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds hold steady in slow London trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds hold steady in slow London trade.

text.p: Dollar-denominated emerging market debt held steady on Friday but trade slowed to a trickle in the absence of significant news.

Dealers said LDC debt, which had shown resilience in the face of weak U.S. Treasuries earlier this week, was now benefiting from the relief of benign U.S. data, allowing many spreads to tighten further.
But retail interest was at a low ebb and business was seen staying slow through the rest of the holiday month of August.

News that Russia had reconciled 71 percent of its debt to the London Club of commercial bank creditors, up only marginally on the 70 percent reported last week, was a shade disappointing but no cause for alarm.
"The point is it's moving in the right direction. At the rate they are going they should be done by the end of September or beginning of October," said the head of trading at a U.S. bank in London.
Russia needs to reconcile 90 percent if the $24 billion principal of its $35 billion total debt to close the deal.
Russian debt was firm with Venshekonombank loans adding 1/8 from New York levels to 102-1/4 while PRINs gained 1/4 to 74-1/8.
Polish Pars were up 1/2 point at 58-7/8.
Among Latin American bonds, Mexico's UMS 2026 gave up some of its strong New York gains, slipping 1/4 to 122.00 while Brazil's "C" bond BR8D14=RR dipped to stand 1/8 lower at 84-1/8.

Argentine FRBs gave up 1/8 to 95-5/8 as Thursday's general strike passed off without serious incident. Support for the stayaway was lukewarm with the government saying 27 percent of workers had observed the strike call in protest at labour law reform plans.
